issues.body:
Part of program #322 / P5, design-only bounded work under U001. This issue prepares concrete source implementation assignments; it does not migrate all capabilities or rewrite validation.

## Problem

The current legacy registry has 16 top-level canonical skills and 95 artifact-kind rows. Those are different inventories, not 95 independent schema files or a commitment to retain every old format. P3 provides five real portable filesystem packages; P4 #341 owns organizational workflows. Remaining reasoning/authoring/context capabilities need explicit portability and ownership dispositions before copying legacy dependencies into src.

Current metadata v1/v2 and distribution.load_package require every public operation to map to an implemented executable tool. That is sufficient for P3 mechanical record operations, but instruction-driven review/design skills need a truthful representation. Do not manufacture a dummy executable or machine-schema obligation for qualitative reasoning merely to fit the current format.

## Exclusive bounded deliverable

Write only `.dev/design/framework-next/capability-consolidation/` and `.dev/workflows/2026-09-23-capability-consolidation/`. Deliver:

1. An evidence-backed inventory of the 16 current canonical skills, their concrete shared/technology/path dependencies, outputs and proposed disposition: portable selectable capability, optional AI-context maintenance, source-only, replacement by an already owned phase, or explicit retirement/unsupported behavior. Preserve useful specialist methods; avoid copying source governance as a downstream requirement.
2. Exact coverage/disposition of the existing 95 artifact-kind registry rows, grouped by actual owner/family with per-kind identity retained. Include the new src schemas and closed metadata/config/manifest/profile/generated-output formats that the legacy registry does not cover. Distinguish source tools, project artifacts, generated observations, external formats and historical records. Propose reader/writer/validator/version/migration ownership for retained formats; no invented approval, execution or compatibility.
3. A minimal contract proposal for instruction-driven versus deterministic tool operations and schema-free outputs. Decide whether a metadata version change is necessary; preserve current v1/v2 semantics. Include concrete examples for one reasoning skill and one schema-owned authoring skill, exact expected package members and source/installed references. No dummy tool or generic plugin engine.
4. Optional AI-context selection: ordinary downstream use must not require audit/governance/init/upgrader/release-closeout. Separate initial installation/update mechanics (P6) from infrequent context maintenance. Keep source-only release/history behavior out of portable bundles.
5. Small, independently owned implementation slices with prerequisites and explicit shared-file owners. P4 source and P6 update/root adoption/P7 checks retain their phases. At least one necessary migration edge must have a future owner and exact candidate input/output versions; explicit unsupported/preserve is valid for retired/historical formats, not a claim that conversion ran.
6. Traditional Chinese explanation of intended user-visible behavior and the work eliminated. Identify overlap with #316, #320, #149/#168 and #274/#275 without closing or silently absorbing those Issues.

## Boundaries and authority

Do not edit src, legacy skills/policies/scripts, root runtime/projections, manifests/profiles, tests, CI, project configuration, shared indexes or coordinator records. Do not move/delete historical files or create a new global runtime registry. This report is a proposal for coordinator selection, not adopted rules, source implementation or Issue closure for other work.

One independent `gpt-6-astra` / `ultra` conversation in the assigned F: worktree. No sub-agents, nested agents or child-created tasks. Coordinator owns integration, shared decisions, future implementation Issues, first push and online PR/merge.

U001 allows only direct UTF-8/JSON/YAML/AST parsing without imports, selected source/reference/Git inspection, diff checks and the exact planned commit-message format check. No product CLIs including help, schema validators, test/fixture/build/package/install/migration trials, audit/lease tooling or CI. Those remain **deferred-by-owner to program #322/P7**. Inventory/source analysis is not runtime coverage. Return coherent local commits and exact HEAD before first push.

No release/tag/publication, credentials, provider mutations or downstream adoption.

issues.body:
## Problem and accepted direction

Manual creation and maintenance of workflow and assessment bundles requires synchronized locator metadata, task records, template versions and index rows. The schema lifecycle assessment ASM-20260921-18-gav observed two preparation failures: workflow references supplied as paths instead of IDs, and an index title that did not exactly match its locator. The owner reviewed the report on 2026-09-21 and authorized proceeding in the proposed sequence.

## Bounded P1 scope

Provide one Python authoring entry point with family-specific operations for AI-context maintenance workflows and AI-context audit assessments. Support deterministic bundle creation, adding tasks, explicit task transitions, controlled locator metadata updates and draft assessment finalization. Reuse canonical templates and existing validator semantics. Provide a minimal capability declaration with explicit readable/writable/migration dispositions; unsupported versions remain rejected without rewriting historical records.

Protect IDs, creation timestamps, assessed subjects and finalized conclusions. Synchronize only the selected index row. Preview planned changes, detect stale inputs, preserve unrelated prose and extension fields, and retain actionable recovery evidence for interrupted multi-file writes. Share mechanical helpers without duplicating semantic authority or claiming multi-file filesystem atomicity.

## Acceptance

1. Minimal semantic inputs produce complete workflow/assessment bundles accepted by existing validators; paths, template versions and index rows are derived.
2. Invalid and missing relations are diagnosed before writing; workflow references use IDs.
3. Title/status/update time changes synchronize the exact index row without rewriting unrelated rows or report prose.
4. Task transitions preserve a single active task and require caller-supplied truthful completion observations; no default creates a passed result.
5. Independent negative tests cover immutable identity/subject/final conclusions, collisions, unknown versions, concurrent edits and path escape.
6. Injected write failures and interruption leave bounded, recoverable evidence; recovery never overwrites external edits.
7. Comments and extension fields have an explicit preservation policy; dry-run changes no tracked files and fixed inputs render deterministically.
8. Compatible optional and incompatible required contract evolution have independent regression oracles.
9. Existing CLI/profile/package registrations remain compatible. Run focused tests and applicable packaging checks, then independent verification on an immutable subject.
10. Deliver an explanation of motivation, behavior changes, retained/relaxed rules, measured mechanics and actual validation limits.

## Boundaries and authorization

Owner authorization: after reviewing the report, the owner said to follow the arranged process and begin the next step. This authorizes local bounded P1 implementation, workflow tracking and applicable verification. P2-P4 broad producer migrations and test/validator removals are deferred. This issue does not authorize push, PR, merge, Issue closure, Project-field changes, release allocation, publication or downstream adoption.

Related: closed #312 and #313; analysis workflow 2026-09-21-schema-artifact-lifecycle. Do not reopen prior issues or absorb #307/#308/#309.

## Problem and authorized next stage

After reviewing the P1 implementation report for #316, the owner approved continuing to P2 from assessment ASM-20260921-18-gav. P1 introduced guarded workflow/assessment authoring while #312 already supplies execution-artifact producers. Common mechanics should have one implementation without merging their distinct parsing, semantic-validation or evidence-custody contracts.

P1 also documented that a valid quoted YAML string such as `Issue #316` is conservatively treated as a comment and blocks authoring updates. P2 will distinguish scalar content from actual comments while preserving the no-silent-comment-loss guarantee.

## Bounded P2 scope

Extract genuinely duplicated strict mapping/parsing and canonical serialization or digest primitives into a small shared portable module. Keep explicit family profiles so authoring JSON/YAML input behavior and existing execution-artifact YAML/anchor/schema behavior remain compatible. Connect the current authoring and execution-artifact producers through that core, and update mandatory authority/dependency/import closure where the new module is part of execution truth. Preserve existing CLIs and family semantic validators.

Implement syntax-aware YAML comment detection for authoring. Accept hashes inside valid scalar content, continue refusing actual comments before rewriting, and retain duplicate-key, key-type, version, alias/tag and immutable-state protections appropriate to each family.

## Acceptance

1. Shared mechanics are implemented once and used by both existing producer families; family-specific semantics remain with their current owners.
2. Existing CLI arguments, successful artifact serialization/digests and failure boundaries remain compatible except the explicitly selected quoted-hash false-positive fix.
3. Independent fixtures prove duplicate and non-string key rejection, family-specific alias/merge/tag and scalar behavior, finite JSON behavior and deterministic serialization.
4. Quoted, plain and block scalar hashes can be edited without losing data; genuine comments still cause refusal before any document mutation, including CRLF and flow/block boundaries.
5. New shared dependencies are included in authority and preview binding and source/package import closure; changed dependencies invalidate stale evidence as required.
6. Focused legacy producer, authoring and packaging smoke checks pass; existing tests and gate identities remain present. No full release/history matrix is implied.
7. Retain workflow progress, failed/blocked observations, an independent fixed-subject verification and a Chinese explanation of changes, preserved/relaxed rules and residual limitations.

## Local integration authorization and boundaries

Owner authorization on 2026-09-21: the P1 report was accepted, the next phase may proceed, existing work may be merged into local main, and branch integrations for this stage should be handled locally because CI is expected to be disrupted by broader changes. This is a task-local exception to the normal hosted PR/CI integration path, not a repository policy rewrite or a claim that CI passed/failed.

P1 was locally merged with its tree unchanged as 9b07d22f80f6ccbe28c1564253e3dab3d3ffad46. P2 uses a new dedicated branch. Local P2 implementation, verification and local integration are authorized; remote push, hosted PR, Issue/Project closure, release/tag/publication and downstream adoption are not included.

P3 other editable families and migration edges, P4 validator/test removal, #307/#308/#309 and reopening #312 remain excluded.
